text:
incident-bot: PAGER — P1: api-prod - sustained 5xx spike in us-east-1, ~18% error rate, routing fallback triggered

devon: I'm on it. Initial observation: spike started after deploy at 10:08 UTC, autoscaler flapped. Rolling back the autoscaler config now.

samir: +1. Confirming rollback started. I'm going to pause Canary->Prod traffic routing to stop new sessions.

devon: rollback applied, pods stabilizing. 5xx dropped to 3% but some requests still timing out. Tracing shows upstream LB health checks failing.

kate: I'm taking LB. Diving into nginx error logs — seeing 502 from backend pool, connection reset. ETA 8m

maria: Noting customer impact: several API customers saw failed completions and increased latency. Billing alert flagged. Notifying support for impacted customers.

support-bot: Alert created: INC-2026-1054. Support assigned: @lia to triage customer messages; template used: "We're investigating an infrastructure incident..."

lia: Reached out to top 5 customers, logged incidents. No data loss reported. They want ETA and postmortem.

samir: After LB fix, adding temporary routing rule to divert traffic to healthy region us-west-2 for non-data-bound requests. Will update routing policy in 2m.

devon: Applied routing policy, 60% of traffic now diverted, overall error rate down to 0.6%.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated — degraded service status. Starting handoff to next on-call. Please fill handoff checklist and schedule postmortem.

devon: Handoff to @kate (next oncall) — summary: autoscaler config regression in deploy -> LB health flapping -> partial region failover. Action items below.

kate: Taking command for post-incident. Can we capture root cause artifacts? logs, deploy diff, autoscaler config. @devon @samir please attach.

devon: Pushed deploy diff to incident doc: https://rwd.company/docs/incidents/2789012345 (internal). Autoscaler config diff:
```
- minReplicas: 2
+ minReplicas: 0
```
This allowed scale-to-zero during rapid traffic change.

samir: LB patch: increased keepalive timeout and fixed health check path. Added temp routing script at /srv/routing/refresh.sh

kate: OK. Actions to track in postmortem:
- A1: Update autoscaler default minReplicas to 2 (owner: devon, due: 2026-06-29)
- A2: Add LB healthcheck integration test (owner: kate, due: 2026-07-02)
- A3: Add runbook step for cross-region diversion and checklist (owner: samir, due: 2026-06-30)
- A4: Support communication follow-up and customer follow-up email (owner: lia, due: 2026-06-29)

Assigning owners and scheduling postmortem slot.

maria: I've added the action items to the incidents board and created PM ticket PM-3812.

kate: Postmortem scheduled: 2026-07-01 16:00 UTC (calendar invite sent). Agenda: timeline, root cause, remediation, runbook updates, verification plan.

devon: I'll draft root cause section and include reproducible test. samir will verify routing automation and apply runbook edits.

samir: Noted. For runbook changes, propose adding a small checklist snippet:
```
# Emergency cross-region diversion
- Confirm downstream data constraints
- Apply routing rule: `rwd-route set --region us-west-2 --percent 50`
- Monitor 5xx and latency for 10m
- Rollback if errors increase
```
Please review and I'll open PR to runbooks repo.

kate: Please open PR with runbook edits and tag oncall-runbook owners. We'll require an oncall pairing to validate automation steps during runway.

lia: Support will send customers a follow-up post-incident note once postmortem is published. I'll add contact logs to the incident doc.

devon: Anything else? If not, I think we can close the pager and run the postmortem cadence.

kate: Sounds good. Closing handoff: owner@oncall - kate; incident doc: https://rwd.company/docs/incidents/2789012345; postmortem meeting invite sent. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Handoff complete. Reminder: update runbook PR and mark actions in incidents board before postmortem.
